Launch the gtregression app

Source: R/gtregression_app.R
gtregression_app.Rd

Open GT Regression, the graphical interface for gtregression: data import and preparation, descriptive tables, regression tables, survival analysis, diagnostics, causal mediation, plots, exports and reproducible R code.

Usage

gtregression_app(..., launch.browser = NULL)

Arguments

...

Additional arguments passed to shiny::runApp(), for example port.

launch.browser

Passed to shiny::runApp(). The default opens the app in your web browser in interactive sessions. Supply a function such as rstudioapi::viewer to choose another viewer.

Value

Invisibly returns the result of shiny::runApp().

Details

gtregression_app() opens GT Regression in your web browser. The RStudio Addin (Addins > GT Regression app) opens exactly the same application in an RStudio dialog window through gtregression_addin(); only the window differs.

The app runs in your local R session, so data frames in your global environment can be chosen from the Data workspace (R Environment). Selected data are copied into the app as read-only snapshots; the source objects are not modified. Files can also be imported, and example data are included.

The app is intentionally kept out of the core package startup path. Shiny and other interface packages are suggested dependencies and are loaded only when gtregression_app() is called.

The Advanced tab includes a guided candidate-model builder. Users can name two to six models, choose model-specific exposures and adjustment variables, optionally add an interaction, and track a primary exposure. The app fits compatible multi_reg(), cox_reg(), or surv_reg() objects before passing them to compare_models(). Generated code records every fitting call and the final comparison for reproducible use outside the app.

See also

gtregression_addin, compare_models(), multi_reg(), cox_reg(), surv_reg()

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  gtregression_app()
}
